err.network: Can’t reach GERMEN Studio. Is it still running?
err.lost: GERMEN Studio no longer knows this training (it may have been restarted).
err.unauthorized: This page is not allowed to talk to GERMEN. Open it again with the address shown by `germen ui`.
err.bad_host: The address of this page is not accepted. Use the address shown by `germen ui`.
err.bad_origin: The request came from another page and was refused.
err.invalid_field: The value of “{field}” is not acceptable.
err.busy: Another job is already running ({kind}). Wait for it to end, or stop it first.
err.model_missing: There is no model called “{name}” to continue.
err.model_busy: This model is being trained right now. Wait for the training to end.
err.bad_name: That name is not allowed. Use letters, digits, “-”, “_” and “.”.
err.denied: GERMEN is not allowed to read that folder.
err.too_large: That file is too large. The limit is {limit}.
err.too_many_files: Too many files with this name in the texts folder. Rename the file and try again.
err.io: A file could not be read or written. {message}
common.copyFailed: Could not copy. Select the text and copy it yourself.
pick.truncated: The list is cut short; this folder has more entries.
pick.hintFolder: Open folders, then choose this folder.
pick.hintModel: Open folders until you find one marked “model”, then select it.
pick.hintFile: Open folders and select a plain-text file.
nav.label: Main menu
shell.trainingNow: Training {name} is running. Open the training page.
shell.offline.title: GERMEN Studio is not answering
shell.offline.text: The program may have been closed. If it is still running, this page reconnects by itself.
quit.title: Quit GERMEN Studio?
quit.textRunning: A training is running. It will be stopped and its model saved, then the program closes.
quit.text: The program will close. Your models and texts stay in the GERMEN folder.
quit.done.title: GERMEN Studio has closed
quit.done.text: You can close this window. To come back, start GERMEN Studio again.
lock.title: This page cannot reach GERMEN
lock.offline: GERMEN Studio is not answering. Start it again (`germen ui`) and open the address it shows.
lock.text: The address is missing its key. Open the full address that `germen ui` prints in the terminal, or start `germen ui` again.
val.int: Enter a whole number from {min} to {max}.
val.numOpen: Enter a number above {min} and up to {max}.
val.name.bad: Use letters, digits, “-”, “_” and “.”, up to 64 characters, starting with a letter or digit.
val.data.uploading: Wait for the upload to finish.
val.warmup: Warm-up cannot be longer than the number of steps.
val.steps.resume: To continue, ask for more steps than the {step} already done.
val.server: The server did not accept this value.
keys.title: Keyboard shortcuts
keys.chartEnds: Jump to the start or end of a chart
models.title: Models
models.lede: Every model you have trained lives in its own folder. Open one to write with it, check it or train it further.
models.openOther: Open a model from another folder
models.empty.title: No model yet
models.empty.text: Train your first one: give GERMEN some text and it grows a small model from scratch.
models.noManifest: This model was saved by an older version and has no checksums, so it cannot be verified.
models.repair.hint: Use “Repair” only if a save was cut off, for example by a power cut. It finishes or discards that save and never touches a good one.
models.repair.completed: An interrupted save was completed ({n} files).
models.repair.discarded: An interrupted save was discarded ({n} files). The previous good state is kept.
gen.title: Write with a model
gen.lede: Pick a model, give it a beginning if you like, and watch it write.
gen.empty.title: Nothing to write with yet
gen.empty.text: Models appear here after they are trained.
gen.modelHint: Saved at step {step}; reads up to {ctx} tokens at once.
gen.beingTrained: This model is being trained right now. GERMEN reads its last saved state.
gen.promptPlaceholder: Start a sentence, or leave this empty and let the model begin.
gen.lengthHint: Number of tokens (bytes, for a byte model).
gen.temperatureHint: Low is cautious and repetitive; high is bold and messy. Around 0.8 is a good start.
gen.topkHint: Only the k likeliest next tokens are considered. 0 means no limit.
gen.windowHint: How much of the text so far the model re-reads at each step (at most {n}). A smaller window is faster.
gen.seedHint: The same seed and settings give the same text. Leave empty for a different text each time.
speed.title: Measure speed
speed.lede: See how fast this computer trains each model size. It takes about a minute.
speed.scalingHint: Repeats the test with different numbers of threads to see how well your processor is used.
speed.threadsBad: Enter whole numbers separated by commas, for example 1, 2, 4, 8.
speed.debug.title: This is a development build
speed.debug.text: Numbers will be many times slower than with a release build. Use the optimised program for real measurements.
speed.measuringText: Each size runs a few real training steps. This takes a moment and uses all your processor cores.
speed.savedText: Measured earlier on this computer; used to estimate how long a training will take.
speed.fig1: How many tokens each size trains on per second. Higher is faster.
speed.estimateHint: The training page uses these numbers to estimate how long a run will take.
speed.scalingLabel: Speed of {preset} by number of threads
speed.fig2: Speed against the number of threads. The dashed line is perfect scaling.
settings.title: Settings
settings.lede: Everything is saved on this computer, in the GERMEN folder.
settings.textSizeHint: Scales all the text and controls.
settings.notify: Notify me when a training ends
settings.notifyHint: A system notification, shown while this window is in the background.
settings.notifyDenied: The browser did not allow notifications.
settings.notifyNone: This browser does not support notifications.
settings.sound: Play a sound when a training is finished
settings.workspaceText: Models, texts and these settings live in this folder. You can back it up or move it like any other.
settings.sessionText: Closing this window does not stop a training: it keeps running until you quit the program.
about.lede: Train a small language model from scratch, on this computer, and watch it learn.
about.privateText: GERMEN Studio talks only to the program on this computer. It sends nothing over the internet, uses no accounts and shows no ads.
about.windowText: This page can only be opened with the secret address printed by the program, and only from this computer.
about.memoryValue: {free} free; a training may use up to {limit}
about.creditsText: GERMEN is free software under the MIT license, written in Rust. It is made by Alexio as part of the trade-free movement.
train.title: Train a model
train.lede: Give GERMEN some text and it grows a small language model from nothing, on this computer. Nothing leaves it.
train.name.title: Name
train.name.label: Name of the model
train.name.hint: It becomes the folder name inside your models folder.
train.mode.label: What to do with the existing model
train.mode.unreadable: “{name}” holds a model that cannot be read
train.mode.unreadableText: You can only replace it, or pick another name.
train.mode.existsText: It is at step {step} with {params} parameters.
train.mode.overwriteWarn: The old model is replaced the first time the new one is saved.
train.data.title: Text to learn from
train.data.demoSub: Built in, made-up sentences. Good for a first try.
train.data.sizeHint: In megabytes. More text takes longer to prepare.
train.data.pathHint: Plain text, UTF-8. More text teaches more.
train.size.title: Model size
train.size.lede: A bigger model can learn more but needs more memory and time. Start small.
train.tok.title: Tokenizer
train.tok.byteHint: Reads the text one byte at a time. Nothing to prepare; works for any language.
train.tok.bpeHint: First learns the most common pieces of your text, so the model reads bigger chunks and learns faster.
train.tok.vocabHint: How many pieces to learn (257 to 65,536).
train.tok.sampleHint: In megabytes. A part of the text is enough.
train.sched.title: How long to train
train.sched.stepsHint: Total number of steps. Each step learns from one batch.
train.sched.lrHint: How big each correction is. 6e-4 suits most cases.
train.sched.warmupHint: Starts gently for this many steps.
train.sched.samples: Show what the model writes while it trains
train.sched.samplesHint: A short sample about every tenth of the way.
train.adv.title: Advanced settings
train.adv.lede: The defaults suit most runs. Change these only if you know why.
train.adv.seqHint: Tokens read at once. 256 if left empty.
train.adv.accumHint: Batches added up before each correction: a bigger effective batch without more memory.
train.adv.minlrHint: The learning rate ends at this fraction of the start (0 to 1).
train.adv.wdHint: Gently shrinks the weights so the model does not just memorise (0 to 1).
train.adv.clipHint: Caps the size of a correction (0 means no cap).
train.adv.valHint: Part of the text never trained on, used to check progress (0 to 0.49).
train.adv.evalEveryHint: Steps between checks on the held-out text (0 never).
train.adv.evalBatchesHint: More batches give a steadier check but take longer.
train.adv.saveEveryHint: Steps between saves (0 saves only at the end).
train.adv.sampleEveryHint: Steps between samples (0 chooses about ten per run).
train.adv.seedHint: The same seed and settings give the same result.
train.est.title: Before you start
train.est.noSpeed: Measure this computer once to see how long a run takes.
train.est.noFit: This may not fit in memory
train.est.noCorpus: The text is too large for this computer
train.est.debugText: Training will be much slower than with the optimised program.
train.replace.title: Replace this model?
train.replace.text: “{name}” will be replaced the first time the new model is saved. This cannot be undone.
train.busy.train: A training is already running. Open it from the menu, or wait for it to end.
train.busy.bench: A speed test is running. Wait for it to end, or stop it on the Speed page.
run.stage.bpe: Learning the pieces of the text
run.hero.noVal: Not checked on the held-out text yet.
run.hero.failed: The training stopped because of an error.
run.stopHint: The model is saved when you stop, so you can continue later.
run.done.title: Training finished
run.done.text: Reached step {step} with a loss of {best}, in {time}. The model is saved.
run.stopped.title: Training stopped
run.stopped.text: Stopped at step {step}. The model is saved, and you can continue from here.
run.stopped.early: Stopped before training began, so nothing was changed.
run.failed.title: Training failed
run.optimizerFresh: The model continues from its saved state, but the optimizer starts fresh because its own state was not found. This is safe; the first steps may look a little bumpy.
run.fig1.title: Loss
run.fig1.label: Loss over the steps of the training
run.fig1.caption: How wrong the model is while it learns. The line is the text it trains on; the dots are the text kept aside for checking. Lower is better.
run.fig2.label: Training speed over time
run.fig2.caption: Tokens handled each second. A steady line means the computer is working evenly.
run.fig3.label: Learning rate over the steps of the training
run.fig3.caption: How big each correction is allowed to be. It rises during warm-up, then slowly falls.
run.fig4.label: Size of the corrections over the steps of the training
run.fig4.caption: How strongly the model is pushed to change. Sudden spikes are a warning sign.
run.spec.title: What the model writes
run.spec.waiting: The first sample appears after the first tenth of the way.
err.timeout: The request took too long to arrive. Try again.
err.bad_version: The Studio does not speak this version of the web protocol.
err.head_too_large: The beginning of the request is too large.
err.length_required: The request did not say how large it is.
err.not_implemented: The Studio does not support this kind of request.
err.uri_too_long: The address of the request is too long.
demo.title: This is a demonstration
demo.text: A real training run, recorded once, is played back here. Nothing is computed on this page and nothing leaves it. To train on your own computer, run GERMEN.
